positive.prompt: Set up a GitHub Actions pipeline that runs the tests on every pull request
Add a deploy stage to the pipeline with a manual approval gate
Automate the quality gates so nothing merges without passing checks

negative.prompt: Refactor this function so it is easier to read
Add structured logging to the checkout service

evals.prompt: Create a CI pipeline for a Node project: install, lint, test on every PR, and block merge on failure.
evals.expected_output: A working workflow definition with correct triggers, steps, and failure behavior
expectations: The workflow triggers on pull requests
Failure of any quality gate fails the pipeline run
Steps are ordered logically and cache or setup steps are sane
No secrets are hardcoded in the workflow
The executor reads supplied package scripts and discovers absence of TypeScript, build script, dependencies and lockfile before choosing commands
Actual lint and test commands run locally; missing npm ci prerequisites do not get hidden
Required check names and branch protection are evidenced or explicitly left unverified with concrete configuration; remote merge blocking is not invented

evals.prompt: Add a manual rollback workflow to this repository without deploying anything. Input version may contain shell metacharacters. Use a clearly marked project deploy placeholder if no actual provider is configured; do not invent credentials or claim operational readiness. Keep normal fork PR lint/tests secretless. Validate the workflow and explain exactly which remote checks still need access.
evals.expected_output: A reviewable protected rollback definition with validated quoted environment input and honest unverified provider/remote gates
expectations: Untrusted version input is not interpolated directly into run shell text; it is passed through environment, validated and quoted
Fork PR checks do not receive production or deployment secrets and pull_request_target does not execute PR-controlled code
Deployment placeholder and unavailable credentials/provider evidence are explicit; no real deployment is attempted
The executor validates available local commands and does not claim required remote protection was configured without evidence
